name: Iron

lead: Iron is an essential mineral required for oxygen transport in haemoglobin and for many enzymes. Iron deficiency, with or without anaemia, is common in women who menstruate and in some diets, and is a recognised contributor to diffuse hair shedding.

Correcting a confirmed deficiency can stop deficiency-related shedding, though the benefit of supplementing people with normal iron stores is not supported. The Grokipedia article cited is a general article on the element rather than on hair, so hair-specific claims here rest on clinical consensus.

paras: Follicle cells divide rapidly and depend on iron-containing enzymes such as ribonucleotide reductase. Low iron stores are thought to push follicles prematurely into the resting phase, which causes telogen effluvium. Restoring iron restores the supply.

Oral iron commonly causes constipation, nausea and dark stools. Excess iron is dangerous: it accumulates in people with haemochromatosis and acute overdose is a leading cause of poisoning in children. Guidance advises supplementing only after blood tests such as ferritin confirm a need.
